speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether he can provide an update on the internal investigations conducted against the Police officers involved in the case of Parti Liyani v PP   SGHC 187.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Generally, the IAO will take this approach: one, look at the facts of the case, the actions of the officers involved, how they have handled any lapses; two, listen to the explanations given by the officers; and three, assess and recommend the disciplinary action, if any, to be taken.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: When the IAO started its investigations against the two officers, I made clear the following two points, which I have made in the past in the House as well as outside.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, our approach must always be to do our duty, conduct investigations without fear or favour.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Second, at the same time, we do not look to scapegoat or act unfairly.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We do not go out to blame and punish, just because there has been a lot of public interest in the matter and because some call for heavy punishment.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We must deal with this case as we would deal with any other case, regardless of publicity.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We must deal with it professionally and properly.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This is important for the public and the Police to know.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Police officers have to often exercise their judgement and discretion in the course of their duties – sometimes on an urgent basis but always under some sort of pressure.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We want our Police officers to be confident in exercising their discretion, when they are performing their duties.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We cannot fault officers, just because we think, with the benefit of hindsight, that we would have exercised our discretion differently in their situation or just because we do not agree with their judgement or exercise of discretion.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And the officers must know that action will be taken against them, only if there are discipline issues or misconduct, or some breach.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The management culture, all the way from the top, must be that we ask that the matter be dealt with fairly, be prepared to explain in public what action is fair and why.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Neglect of duty means the failure to take proper action to perform a required task.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The penalty for neglect of duty depends on the officers' degree of culpability and the harm caused by their actions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Penalties can range from a reprimand, or financial penalty, to demotion and dismissal from service.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The maximum financial penalty imposed under the Public Service Commission (Delegation of Disciplinary Functions) Directions is a fine equivalent to the stoppage of increment for two years.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are, of course, other more severe penalties possible, under legislation, and that really depends on the conduct.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The IO who handled the Police report handled it as a routine theft case; and it was so.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, the IO did not visit the scene of crime promptly to carry out investigation and gather evidence.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This contributed to a break in the chain of custody for some exhibits.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Second, the IO did not properly verify some of the claims made by the parties during the investigation.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Third, his supervisor did not provide sufficient guidance, which contributed to the lapses.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The IAO also took into account the intense pressure that the IO was working under.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He was handling many ongoing investigations, prosecutions and conducting arrest operations at the same time.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I have spoken before about the workload challenges that Police IOs face.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The only way to deal with this is to increase Police's headcount.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is a difficult problem and not easily solvable because of the general manpower shortage.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As I said, the two Police officers were doing their jobs under difficult circumstances and, up until this incident, they have discharged their duties dutifully.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I have sympathy for the situation that they find themselves in.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But they have fallen short of expectations, and they have been dealt with in the way other officers would have been dealt with in similar circumstances.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am heartened to see that we are putting our officers at the heart, front and centre of the things that we do, even during investigations.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They face pressures of family, professionally and personally as well.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am heartened that there is some form of review on the workload distribution and the manpower challenges.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In this regard, may I ask if there are any avenues for our officers to escalate the pressures of the workload or the stressors that they are facing, both at work and elsewhere, within the institution of the Police organisation and the investigation body?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, whether or not there could be a bit more support in terms of counselling, mentorship, perhaps?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I note that the supervisor in this case has been found to have lapsed in his supervision, but could there have been other channels of oversight or avenues for the officer to escalate those stressors and the pressures that he may face?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: First, we put the officers at the heart of what we do because there is something even more central and fundamental – which is public interest.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The officers are there to serve public interest and if public interest is affected in some way, we have to take action.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But the institution can only do well if the officers are treated fairly.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The officers have to be treated fairly so that they can do their job and so that public interest – which is the fundamental, primary, central goal – is achieved.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, it is not putting officers above the public but serving the public through making sure that there is a strong institution.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And in order for there to be a strong institution, there have got to be good officers who know that they will be treated fairly.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the second point, how do we take care of the officers, there are many avenues.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In every context, there are officers' senior officers who are tasked to take feedback, collect, understand and, in fact, part of leadership, that has to be emphasised – not just in SPF, but in other places, too – is to make sure that the morale of your officers remains high.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Contrary to the way people perceive police forces in many other parts of the world, the Singapore Police officer is held in very high esteem, very high regard.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As to whether we can do more, I have explained the difficulties.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The fundamental difficulty is that there are not enough officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There is only so much more that you can do when your central problem is that there is more work than can reasonably be done by the workforce we have.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I have said we do our best in those circumstances.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister on what he just told the House.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, he mentioned that the punishment that was recommended for the two officers, meaning the IO and his supervisor, was a fine which was equivalent to a stoppage of pay, or something along those lines.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to ask him whether he means that the officers concerned will not receive their pay for a few months.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question is, were the IO and the supervisor punished similarly?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In other words, was one assigned more responsibility than the other and will one have stoppage of more months of pay compared to the other?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, there were actually two penalties imposed on them.
